title: Geometry - Lesson 4 Assessment: Rectangular Prism Volume
description: Solve rectangular prism volume tasks with labeled units.

questions.question: A prism has length 5 cm, width 4 cm, and height 3 cm. What is its volume?
A box is 10 cm long, 4 cm wide, and 6 cm high. What is its volume? Enter just the number.
The height of a prism tells how many layers are stacked.
questions.explanation: Height is the number of layers when modeling with unit cubes.

questions.question: A prism has base area 24 square units and height 7 units. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume = base area × height = 24 × 7 = 168 cubic units.

questions.question: A prism is 9 m long, 3 m wide, and 4 m high. What is its volume? Enter just the number.
A student calculates 8 × 3 = 24 cm² for a box that is 8 cm by 3 cm by 5 cm. What did the student find, and what is the correct volume?
questions.correctAnswer: The student found the base area. The correct volume is 8 × 3 × 5 = 120 cm³.
questions.explanation: The student omitted height. Volume needs all three dimensions and cubic units.

questions.question: A prism has volume 180 cm³, length 9 cm, and width 4 cm. What is its height? Enter just the number.
Which measurement set gives a volume of 120 cubic units?
Explain how unit-cube layers show why V = l × w × h.
questions.correctAnswer: Length × width counts cubes in one base layer, and multiplying by height counts all stacked layers.
questions.explanation: The formula comes from layer counting: base layer cubes times number of layers.

questions.question: A rectangular aquarium is 30 cm long, 10 cm wide, and 20 cm high. Find its volume with units.
